title: Activation recoder: INT8 calibration pipeline and runtime kernel fallback
creator: Liam Chen
description: Implement a production-ready 'activation recoder' workflow that computes per-layer activation recoding factors for INT8 deployment (activation-side scaling) and integrates those profiles into the runtime so kernels can apply fast rescale paths or safely fall back to FP16/FP32 when mismatch/overflow is detected.
background: We've observed per-workload activation distribution drift for KV-cache-heavy chat workloads and for long-sequence prompts. Existing static per-layer scales reduce accuracy on a subset of benchmarks. This ticket designs a deployable calibration pipeline that emits compact recoding profiles, validates accuracy against representative eval sets, and wires up runtime kernel shims to choose optimized microkernels or safe fallbacks based on profile/runtime signals.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end pipeline that takes model checkpoints and representative request traces and outputs a compact recode profile artifact; 2) Runtime accepts profile artifact and enables zero-downtime activation rescaling with <1% mean token-level quality regression vs baseline FP16 on the repro eval suite; 3) Kernel selector chooses optimized INT8 path for supported GPUs and falls back to FP16/FP32 without correctness loss; 4) Telemetry surfaces per-route quantization failures and accuracy regressions in Console.
tasks: Design profile schema (compact per-layer multipliers + versioning + seed/hash) and storage format
Implement calibration harness to ingest representative traces and compute recoding factors (batch-aware)
Add unit/regression tests for synthetic activation distributions and known edge cases (very large outliers)
Extend model onboarding to store profile artifact in model catalog with compatibility matrix
Implement runtime profile loader and a microkernel selector with safety checks (overflow detection/KV-cache mismatch)
Wire Console telemetry for profile application success, kernel path metrics, and per-route eval deltas
Create rollout plan (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on quality regression thresholds
implementation_notes: We will emit profiles as gzipped protobufs (v1) for compactness and forward compatibility. Calibration will compute geometric mean scaling for cross-layer energy balance and will optionally produce per-channel multipliers for matmul ops where supported. For runtime, add a light-weight verification step: sample N warmup tokens and check accumulators for out-of-range signals before switching to INT8 kernels. If verification fails, runtime should gracefully continue in FP16.
perf_results: Preliminary calibration on wizard-chat trace: LLM-small => 3.2% token perplexity reduction vs naive static scale
Latency: INT8 fast path microkernel shows 18-22% lower p95 token latency on A100 vs FP16 for 2k sequence workloads in local tests
Throughput: 1.25-1.4x tokens/sec improvement on batched infer with INT8 kernels under controlled traces
Quality: On repro eval set (n=1200 prompts), mean exact-match delta vs FP16 = 0.8% (within target <1%)
risks_mitigations: Risk: Activation outliers during real traffic causing saturation. Mitigation: runtime dynamic verify and auto-fallback to FP16 for the request and flagged route

Risk: Profile mismatch for customer-provided traces that don't represent production. Mitigation: require profile provenance metadata and expose warnings in Console when traffic diverges from calibration trace signatures
Risk: Kernel compatibility across GPU families. Mitigation: maintain compatibility matrix and use generic fallback microkernels when optimized kernels unavailable
comments: 2025-02-18 - LC: Created ticket and linked initial design doc. Prototype calibration script produced candidate profiles for 3 models.
2025-02-20 - AP: Implemented profile schema and wrote ingestion tests. Pushed experimental loader to runtime branch, awaiting perf numbers.
2025-02-22 - MG: Design review notes: prefer geometric mean scaling to simple max-based rescale for better numeric stability; add provenance hash to profile header.

2025-02-24 - NB: Ran long-seq KV-cache chat traces; observed INT8 fast-path failure on 1% of sessions due to unexpected outlier tokens. Added warmup verification gate to runtime. Re-ran tests, failure rate dropped to 0.02%.
2025-02-26 - AP: Integration tests green on internal CI (linux-a100). Preparing canary rollout patch and support doc for on-call about telemetry alerts.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge calibration and runtime loader PRs behind feature flag; 2) Canary on internal sandbox (5% internal traffic) for 48h; 3) Expand to <customer tier 'developer' routes> 10% for one week with close monitoring; 4) Apply automated QA: if Console reports >1% quality regression or >0.1% saturation events, immediate rollback; 5) Full rollout after 2 weeks stability or manual sign-off
monitoring_alerts: Console alert thresholds: quant_fail_rate > 0.1% over 1h, average eval_delta > 1% over 6h, kernel_error_rate > 0.05% over 15m
notes_for_oncall: If Console shows quant_fail_rate spike, flip feature flag for affected shard, gather last 500 traces, run quick check script (scripts/quant/verify_profile.sh) and escalate to quant infra on-call.
postmortem_plan: If a rollout triggers regression, collect traces + profile used, reproduce locally with calib harness, generate a minimal repro, and file a postmortem linked to this ticket with root cause and fix timeline.
